family.name: Founder's Office / Chief of Staff
family.summary: The board meets in three days and every team says its numbers look great: find the growth that is losing money on each order, pick one priority for next quarter, and fix a cherry-picked board slide.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: The three numbers that matter
stages.summary: Pull the real story from four teams' numbers: growth bought with discounts, money lost per order, a shrinking runway. Think aloud.

stages.title: One priority for next quarter
stages.summary: Recommend one company priority. Tests judgement with cash at stake. Think aloud.

stages.title: After the board meeting
stages.summary: Reactions to their priority. Tests adapting and handling people.

stages.title: Review marketing's board slide
stages.summary: A board slide with an inflated CAC claim, revenue without returns and no comparison point. Think aloud.

stages.title: The board note (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the CEO's one-page board note with AI. Catches spin and invented numbers.

stages.title: Something you drove across teams
stages.summary: A real piece of work they drove across teams without authority. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You work in the founder's office at **Nuvo Skin**, a skincare brand selling online. The CEO messages: **"Board meeting in three days. Tell me the three numbers that really matter and what our one priority for next quarter should be."**
What each team sent you (this quarter vs last)

rows: Cost to acquire a new customer down 22%. Average discount 12% → 26%.
Shipping cost per order down 9%. Returns 8% → 16% of orders (most say "damaged in transit").
Profit per order after product, shipping, discounts and marketing: ₹110 → -₹30. Monthly cash burn ₹1,00,00,000 → ₹1,56,00,000. Cash in bank ₹14,00,00,000.

brief.text: A note from Finance: marketing's "new customers" count includes anyone using a new-customer coupon; about 39% of those were existing customers with a new email. Runway at the old burn was about 14 months.
The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a time you had to make sense of a lot of information quickly.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Which three numbers would you put in front of the board, and what story do they tell together?** Say which team numbers you don't trust, and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Keep pushing growth with discounts to look strong for fundraising
Cut discounts and fix the money lost on each order, even if growth slows
Start fundraising now, before the numbers get worse

prompt.text: **What one priority do you recommend for next quarter?** Pick one, give the reasoning with numbers, and say what the company should stop doing.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Keep pushing growth with discounts to look strong for fundraising"

prompt.text: A board member asked about unit economics, and the CEO couldn't answer well. The board asks for a plan to break even per order within two quarters.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Cut discounts and fix the money lost on each order, even if growth slows"

prompt.text: Discounts were cut. Profit per order is back above zero, but revenue fell 14% this month. The Growth head tells the CEO you "killed the momentum" and the team is demotivated.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Start fundraising now, before the numbers get worse"

prompt.text: Three investors passed, all citing unit economics. Runway is now down a month, and the CEO is spending all their time on fundraising.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Fix the returns problem first"

prompt.text: Switching couriers takes 8 weeks. Meanwhile discounts are still at 26% and burn hasn't moved. The CEO asks why nothing has changed.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: The marketing head wants this slide in the board deck. **Name the problems, worst first, and what the board would wrongly conclude from each.** Then say what the slide should show.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: Revenue **₹8,60,16,000**, our highest ever (orders × average order value).
Chart: monthly revenue, last three months only.
Sources: our ad platforms and the store's order system.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the one-page note the CEO sends the board before the meeting (under 250 words): what happened this quarter, the three numbers, the priority and what will change.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.
